newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria sets up oil industry monitoring groups.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sets up oil industry monitoring groups.

text.p: Nigeria on Thursday set up committees to monitor its joint venture operations with multinational oil firms and the implementation of its $4 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project.
Oil minister Dan Etete, speaking in the capital Abuja, said that the two committees would ensure Nigeria receive the maximum return from the oil industry, its economic lifeblood.

The move follows comments made last year by Etete when he said Nigeria was not in firm control of its oil industry, which is run by multinational oil firms, and needed to take control of the situation.

Most of Nigeria's two million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil is produced by the multinationals which operate in joint ventures in which state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) has a majority stake.
NNPC contributes to their operations to the tune of its equity, which averages 60 percent, in the joint ventures -- costing Nigeria about $2 billion annually in cash calls.
Etete said one of the committees inaugurated on Thursday would focus solely on the joint ventures.

He said it will "ensure the establishment of joint accounts for each of the joint ventures with the central bank whereby each partner contributes its cash calls and subsequently monitor the management of accounts."

It would also undertake market intelligence of the cost of equipment to ensure prices were not inflated to Nigeria's detriment and check that jobs that should be done by Nigerians and Nigerian firms are not given to foreigners, he said.
It would also ensure taxes due to the government were paid.
The second committee will focus on the LNG project "ensuring the maximisation of local content in the award of contracts and services in the industry including subcontracts," Etete said.
The oil companies were not immediately available to comment on the committees, made up of Nigerian oil ministry officials.
Among the main foreign oil companies in Nigeria are the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Chevron Corp, Mobil Corp, Texaco Inc, Agip SpA and Elf Aquitaine.
